open_obligations: Note that ICM is unsupervised elicitation, not easy-to-hard finetuning.
Check whether golden labels on author gender are themselves reliable.
Note this is one task with 100 test examples for the human baseline.
in.other_title: ICM elicits superhuman author-gender prediction: 80% vs 60% for human labels
in.rationale: Hase et al. state their easy-to-hard results are limited to tasks humans label reliably and may not hold where humans cannot produce accurate labels. Wen et al. report a task where 5 human annotators are consistent but only 60% accurate while ICM matches golden labels at 80%; evaluation still uses golden labels, so the test setting itself has ground truth.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether capabilities can be elicited on tasks where human labels are unreliable, for author-gender prediction where humans reach 60%

text: The authors state that because ground truth labels are needed to evaluate generalization, their evaluations are limited to datasets humans have reliably labeled, and that their results may not generalize to other difficulty levels, especially test settings where almost no human effort can produce accurate labels, such as unsolved scientific questions.
title: Easy-to-hard results limited to tasks with reliable human labels
